messages:
Maya (CS): FYI — CoralHealth renewal in ~6 weeks. We saw onboarding latency regressions last week; customer is asking for a clean SLA/SLO summary + potential credit exposure by EOD Fri. Sharing initial notes and dashboard link: https://redwood.ops/dashboards/coralhealth/slo

Maya (CS): Quick context — they agreed to: uptime 99.9% (monthly), p95 latency < 600ms. Last week p95 jumped to ~1.2s for ~1.8% of requests during a 1h window. Need agreed numbers (uptime/latency achieved), root cause, and proposed credit/write-off.

Jorge (SRE): I pulled traces — spike coincides with KV cache invalidation during a config roll at 03:10 UTC on 2026-03-12. Root cause: cache TTL rollout + a noisy canary that missed the feature flag.

Jorge (SRE): Logs snippet: ```stderr
2026-03-12T03:09:58Z cache:ttl_update id=kv-42 applied=false
2026-03-12T03:10:12Z request:latency p95=1210ms route=/v1/generate
2026-03-12T04:10:15Z request:latency p95=580ms route=/v1/generate
```

Tom (Eng-Infra): I can push a patch to ensure rolling updates drain existing cache keys before TTL changes. Will also add a temporary guard to prevent canaries from flipping TTL concurrently. ETA 48h unless we cut a hotfix branch now.

Priya (CS Ops): For comms we need: 1) exact achieved uptime/latency for the billing month, 2) a simple credit calc, 3) remediation actions + timeline, 4) internal owner for follow-up. I can draft a customer note once we have numbers.

Leah (Product): Re: credit calc — recommend following standard playbook: offer a one-time credit equal to X% of monthly invoice where X = min(5%, floor((SLO_target - achieved_uptime)/0.001)*5%). Example we send: if target 99.9% and achieved 99.85% -> shortfall 0.05% -> credit = floor(0.0005/0.001)*5% = 0% (so no credit). For larger shortfalls we round down by 0.1% buckets. We can be more generous for renewal risk customers; ping me if we want to go outside playbook.

Maya (CS): Hmm that rounding behavior might under-count small but meaningful hits. CoralHealth is flagged as high-touch. Suggest we calculate both strict-playbook credit and a goodwill credit tier for negotiations. Priya, can you prepare both numbers?

Priya (CS Ops): Yep — I'll compute: (a) playbook calc, (b) goodwill proposal (capped at 10% invoice). Need monthly invoice total from billing — @Leah can you confirm revenue tier / monthly fee?

Leah (Product): CoralHealth is on enterprise plan — monthly invoice = $48,000.

Priya (CS Ops): Draft calc: achieved uptime (billing month) = 99.82% (preliminary from infra dashboard). Shortfall = 0.08% -> playbook buckets 0.08% rounded down to 0.0% (0 credit) per current floor rule. Goodwill proposal: 5% credit of $48k = $2,400. I'll produce both numbers with exact breakdown and put in the comms draft.

Jorge (SRE): Confirmed the 1h degradation pushed overall monthly uptime from 99.90% -> ~99.82% for that customer because their traffic distribution weighted that hour higher. I can produce the per-hour availability table for the month.

Tom (Eng-Infra): I'll scope the hotfix now; if we cut a targeted patch and deploy within 24h we can avoid recurrence before renewal. If we need emergency rollout I can lead the change and coordinate canary gating.

Maya (CS): Action items: 
- Jorge: export hourly availability + p95 table and attach to thread (ETA 3h)
- Tom: confirm hotfix plan & ETA (48h normal / 8h emergency)
- Priya: draft customer note with playbook + goodwill numbers (ETA EOD today)
- Leah: confirm revenue/approval for goodwill credit (reply here)

Tom (Eng-Infra): Acknowledged — I'll post a short runbook change: ```bash
# temp guard to prevent concurrent TTL flips
kubectl label nodes edge-*/no-ttl-flip=true
# patch rollout
kubectl apply -f ttl-guard.yaml --record
```

Leah (Product): Approved to offer up to 5% goodwill credit for CoralHealth without exec escalation. If CS wants to go to 10% we need revenue signoff.

Priya (CS Ops): Draft ready, attaching snippet below and will add numbers when Jorge posts final table:
"Dear Cor alHealth team — we observed a regrettable latency incident during onboarding that impacted p95 for a short window. Per our SLA, we calculated the monthly uptime and the corresponding credit under the standard playbook. As a goodwill gesture given your renewal timing, we propose a one-time credit of $2,400 while we finalize remediation. Full incident report and corrective actions to follow."

Maya (CS): This is great. Once Jorge drops the table I'll finalize and send to legal for quick review then outbound to the customer.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3043 — SRE investigating cache TTL rollout impact on latency. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-3043

Jorge (SRE): Table uploaded to the dashboard and attached here: https://redwood.ops/reports/coralhealth/2026-03-availability.csv

Priya (CS Ops): Final numbers computed: monthly uptime 99.82%; p95 aggregated = 710ms; playbook credit = $0; goodwill credit offered = $2,400 (5%). Draft note updated.

Maya (CS): Sending to legal now. Will loop back with customer after legal ok. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
